articles.title: Alan Wake 2: Deluxe Edition for PS5 Drops to Its Lowest Price Ever, Just in Time for Halloween
articles.summary: IGN's best horror game of 2023.
articles.body:
There are few things better during the Halloween season than immersing yourself in a fright fest of a game. Right on cue, Amazon has discounted the excellent Alan Wake 2: Deluxe Edition PlayStation 5 game to the lowest price ever. You can pick up a physical copy for just $29.95. That's $5 cheaper than the previous low, which we saw on Black Friday of 2025.

Alan Wake 2: Deluxe Edition (PS5) Drops to the Lowest Price Ever

Alan Wake 2 was released almost exactly three years ago, on October 27, 2023. In addition to Tristan Ogilvie's glowing Alan Wake 2 IGN review , the game also ranked as our best horror game of 2023 . Alan Wake 2 mixes survival horror 3rd-person action gameplay with immersive live action cutscenes with really high production values. There are very few games quite like it. The horror is mostly psychological, but there are plenty of visceral jump scares along the way. I generally don't have the stomach for horror games and, sadly, this game was too scary for me to completely finish.

The Deluxe Edition includes the base game, the Night Springs and Lake House story expansions, both of which have already been released, and a remastered digital edition of the original Alan Wake game.

Eric Song is the IGN commerce manager in charge of finding the best gaming and tech deals every day. When Eric isn't hunting for deals for other people at work, he's hunting for deals for himself during his free time.

articles.title: Before There Was Heated Rivalry, There Was Yuri!!! On Ice
articles.summary: Ten years later, the anime Yuri!!! On Ice remains special – and groundbreaking.
articles.body:
When the finale of Yuri!!! On Ice (hereafter YOI) dropped on December 21, 2016, demand for watching and discussing the episode was so high that Crunchyroll and Tumblr crashed. The moment was the culmination of a 12-week period on the internet that started with cautious excitement for YOI’s October premiere—mostly from within the online anime community and sparked by a few promotional trailers —and snowballed from there. In a time before the Thai BL drama boom, or the release of English-language romances like Heartstopper and Heated Rivalry , YOI broke anime containment by depicting a world in which queer characters were not just featured, but were allowed joy, low-stakes intimacy, and a happy ending. Ten years later, it’s still special.

Yuri!!! On Ice begins when protagonist Yuri Katsuki (Toshiyuki Toyonaga) is at his lowest. A 23-year-old competitive ice skater struggling with anxiety and depression, he has just returned home to coastal Japan following a humiliating season. Yuri is seriously considering quitting the sport altogether when his idol and fellow competitor, Russia’s Victor Nikiforov (Junichi Suwabe), shows up at Yuri’s family onsen and volunteers to be his new coach. As the 12-episode season progresses, Yuri builds confidence in himself as a skater and a human, falling in love with Victor along the way.

Many of YOI’s initial watchers were intrigued by the figure skating subject, which felt unique as a subject in sports anime—or live-action TV drama, for that matter. “I love figure skating, so when I saw the news that a new sports anime about figure skating was coming, I was excited,” a 34-year-old European fan named Toblerone tells me of first watching YOI in 2016. “When the first episode aired, I was glued to my monitor. The episode was magical, and so much better than I had even dreamed. It was love at first sight.” Others were drawn in by the character design, animation style, and music teased in the promotional videos. Some were already fans of co-creator Sayo Yamamoto, who had previously directed Michiko & Hatchin and Lupin the Third: The Woman Called Fujiko Mine. (Yamamoto co-directed the series alongside Jun Shishido, and co-wrote it with Mitsurō Kubo.)

And, of course, there were those looking for more queer representation in their media. In 2016, it was more common for pop culture to queerbait than to depict explicitly queer relationships. Before the series premiered and in its first half, most viewers assumed any potential queerness would be kept as subtext. While anime had depicted queer characters and relationships before, such as in Revolutionary Girl Utena or No. 6, it was not common to see a queer relationship made canon in a mainstream sports anime. RedSkyLine, another online YOI fan who watched the show in 2016, calls the series fundamental to TV history. “I really think modern LGBT storytelling owes a lot to YOI,” they told me, adding that media today is “less ashamed of showing a more gentle side of male characters.” RedSkyLine was the same age as Yuri when the series originally aired, and the character helped them feel seen, represented, and “taught me what love is like.”

The Best Anime of the Decade (2010 - 2019)

For Americans especially who did not seek out foreign-language media, anime might not have seemed like a particularly queer space. Some of the first anime series to be broadcast in the U.S., Sailor Moon and Cardcaptor Sakura , were censored to downplay or remove queer storylines altogether. In 2016, anime was only starting to become mainstream in the U.S., where animation more broadly had historically been viewed as a less complex medium, made solely for children. Anime in particular was seen as a boys thing, in part because of import decisions in the 1990s and 2000s that prioritized shonen series like Dragon Ball Z, One Piece, and Naruto. Crunchyroll, which had launched in 2006 as a pirate site specializing in East Asian content before committing to legal licensing in 2009, was starting to complicate that perception, but it was still relatively uncommon for people in the U.S. to watch foreign-language media.

But the lines between international media markets were blurring, spurred along by the growth of streamers and social media-driven fan culture that made accessing and discussing foreign-langauge media with other fans much easier. In 2016, Crunchyroll saw a 36% surge in paid subscribers . In 2017, they hit one million paid subscribers (compared to 21 million in 2026 ).

Yuri!!! On Ice contributed to that expansion. It was easily the most tweeted about anime of the fall 2016 season, getting 1,440,596 mentions on the platform. (For comparison, the runner up—Haikyu!, another sports anime with an exclamation point in its name—had 348,109 mentions in the same time frame.) For many Western viewers—perhaps especially girls, women, and queer folks—it changed the perception of what an anime could be, and who it was for.

In an internet era when Tumblr could build entire fan empires, YOI was inescapable on the fan platform. When Yuri and Victor apparently kiss in Episode 7 of the series (the lip-lock is obscured by Victor’s arm, but is broadly accepted as canon), fans on Twitter and Tumblr put out the Bat Signal: Here be queer, comforting media. Episode reaction convinced many who had yet to give the series a chance to finally try it ( including future Olympic skater Amber Glenn ). “I remember everyone talking about it and what convinced me was the entire world going crazy over the Episode 7 kiss when it dropped. I saw even people I knew irl who I didn't even know were into anime posting about it,” says Naghi, a 25-year-old fan from Italy. “[I] decided it was time [to check out YOI], considering I was also a fan of figure skating.”

Ten years later, YOI often gets recommended to fans of queer media, as it should, but its success as a series doesn’t come down to just one element. A sports anime first and foremost, the series is focused on depicting the inner worlds of male figure skaters competing at the highest international level, and often uses different animation styles to give viewers insight into a particular performer's mindset during a routine. We are introduced to skaters from Thailand, Canada, Switzerland, the Czech Republic, Italy, Kazakhstan, China, the U.S., and of course Japan and Russia, as these athletes seek to express themselves artistically in the ultimate display of mental and physical resilience.

“I loved the representation, seeing characters from all over the world treated with love, all the way to their music choices,” says Em, a 31-year-old non-binary fan from the American Midwest. “It was cool to have an anime with a diverse cast and a soundtrack to match.” Em rewatches YOI every winter, when seasonal depression hits. “It’s a story of love and hope and friendship and community, and it has and continues to get me through dark times in my life,” they say. “It was unapologetically queer when I was first coming to terms with my own identity, and when I first saw it, I thought: if even a mainstream anime like this can be queer, surely it’s okay that I am too.”

The series employed Japanese figure skater Kenji Miyamoto to choreograph the many routines in the series, giving the anime a deeper, sport-specific authenticity. As part of the production process, Miyamoto recorded himself performing the routines; the recordings were used for both reference and in the sound design. The scrapes and crunches heard as characters rip, glide, and spin across the ice are from Miyamoto. This deep respect for its subject matter garnered recognition from real-life ice skaters, including Johnny Weir, Adam Rippon, and Evgenia Armanovna Medvedeva. “History Maker,” YOI’s opening theme , was played during the opening ceremony of the Grand Prix of Figuring Skating in Nagoya, and Japanese pair skaters Ryuichi Kihara and Miu Suzaki performed to “Yuri On Ice” at the 2018 Winter Olympics.

For Maggie, an academic and YOI fan fiction writer, the world has changed a great deal since the anime’s release, but that makes its existence all the more vital. “There's been a global rise of fascism and far right thinking around the globe that's a direct response to the kind of social progress that YOI represents,” she says. “This extends to all arenas. On the flip side, progress pushes forward regardless, and shows like Heated Rivalry prove the concept that YOI laid out: queer sports representation is fundamental.”

Despite its massive success and enduring legacy, YOI has yet to get a second season. A prequel film focused on Victor and titled Yuri!!! On Ice the Movie: Ice Adolescence was announced in 2017, with a trailer released in 2019 . However, animation studio MAPPA officially canceled the project in 2024 due to “various circumstances.” In 2025, producer Hideo Katsumata told Animehunch that the movie never came together due to creative differences. Still, many fans remain hopeful. In January 2026, Netflix announced a strategic partnership with MAPPA to co-produce and globally distribute anime projects. Following the success of YOI, MAPPA went on to produce other popular titles, including Jujutsu Kaisen, Chainsaw Man, and the final season of Attack on Titan.

“If this show were to come back, the fandom would revive and its comeback would break the internet,” says Alexis, a 22-year-old fan from Kentucky. She watched the series in 2016, after hearing friends rave about it, but has seen new generations of anime fans discovering YOI over the years as it becomes accessible on different streaming platforms. “I feel that edits are very popular as of right now. I've seen SOOO many edits with 600,000+ likes and every comment is people who have waited for years, still hoping we see them again.”

In the meantime, YOI fans will continue to be inspired by the groundbreaking sports anime, showing their love through rewatches, trips to Japan, sharing with friends, and the creation of transformative fanworks. “It is one of the pieces of media that I always keep coming back to, no matter how many times I take a break in other fandoms,” says Mia, a 29-year-old fan. “It’s been with me through a lot of stages of my life: heading off abroad to uni, getting stuck with my family during Covid, and still now a full decade after I first learned it existed. I know I’ll be rewatching it a decade from now, too.”

articles.title: Birdbuddy’s budget feeder foiled my squirrels
articles.summary: Birdbuddy’s newest smart bird feeders are cheaper, faster, and sleeker, but the new camera might be a deal-breaker for diehard birders.
articles.body: Birdbuddy’s next-generation smart bird feeders have finally arrived. After spending a few days with the BirdBuddy Nook (from $99) and longer with the flagship Birdbuddy Home ($219), there’s a clear winner: The Nook is the perfect all-rounder, just the right blend of technology, nature, and value to bring you delightful scenes from the lives of your backyard birds. But — and this is a pigeon-sized but — the new camera on both the Nook and the Home is a bit of a downgrade compared to the Birdbuddy Pro ($339, but often on sale for less). It has slightly worse viewing angles, the 2K HDR image quality isn’t as crisp or bright, and you now have to remove the whole feeder to charge it. On the plus side, you can now rotate the new camera to capture a wide-angle 135-degree landscape view. The live feed loads much faster in the Birdbuddy app thanks to a new instant wake-up feature. In testing, the livestream appeared in under eight seconds, compared to about 30 on the Pro. That’s the difference between seeing a bird up close in real time and watching its tail feathers fly away. [Image: The Birdbuddy Nook (left) with optional perch extender ($43), and the Birdbuddy Home (right). For those unfamiliar, smart bird feeders use an AI-powered camera to capture photos and videos of visiting feathered friends (and the occasional unwanted furry beast). First announced at CES in January under different names, the Birdbuddy Nook and Birdbuddy Home follow the company’s hugely successful Birdbuddy (2022) and Birdbuddy Pro (2024). They have completely new designs featuring the new camera, but the headline feature is that both are more affordable than the Pro, which Birdbuddy has now discontinued. (It’s currently selling for $239.99 on Amazon.) New tech that’s cheaper? In 2026? Bravo, Birdbuddy. [Product: Birdbuddy Nook | [Product: Birdbuddy Home | [Product: Birdbuddy Pro (solar) | Birdbuddy’s new camera is the biggest change, but it comes with some compromises. As you can see in the videos below, the new portrait mode has a slightly narrower view of the feeder than the Pro, so while you get close-ups, the bird’s face can get cut off if it’s standing on the edge of the feeder. In the new landscape mode (which the Pro doesn’t offer), the view cuts off the seed tray. So, while you get a wider view that’s better for seeing more bird activity, you no longer see the feed tray — resulting in more feathers but fewer up-close faces. [Video: BirdBuddy Testing 1] [Video: Bird Buddy Testing 2] Despite the reduced angle and less vivid color, the camera is still very good; the images are clear and colorful, with plenty of detail, and the company says it’s optimized for better action and low-light shots — though I haven’t seen that in my testing. I also really like the landscape option; it’s one of the reasons I enjoyed the Coolfly model I tested earlier this year. While portrait gives you an intimate up-close look, landscape captures more of the scene, including birds in flight and interacting. (You have to manually change the angles by repositioning the camera; you can’t do it through the app.) [Media: A montage of videos from the Home (blue tray/red perch) and the Nook (green tray/white perch) in portrait and landscape views. Birdbuddy’s excellent app shows you the videos and photos the camera captures in a fun “feed,” where you can scroll through all your backyard visitors and manually initiate free, AI-powered species identification. To have the app automatically identify birds, you need a subscription ($7.99 a month or $69.99 a year), which also lets you name returning visitors and put silly augmented-reality hats on them, which was a lot more fun than I expected. Birdbuddy’s identification has been very good overall, though I’ve noticed the new camera struggles to identify some smaller, faster birds compared to the Pro. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: While the camera is the same on the Home and Nook, the feeders differ. The easiest way to sum this up is maintenance. The Home is more hands-off: it holds six cups of seed compared to just under four on the Nook, has built-in solar, so you won’t have to take it down to charge as often, and supports 5 GHz Wi-Fi, while the Nook is only 2.4 GHz. The Home is also slightly bigger, with a larger seed tray, so it may attract larger birds. In addition to the $99 base model, the Nook has two models with add-ons that bring it closer to the Home feature-wise: Nook Solar for $159 (with only one panel compared to two on the Home), and the Nook Extended Edition for $199, with solar and a perch extender to accommodate more visitors (you can buy the perch separately for $43). That’s the model I’m testing, but it’s just $20 less than the Home. If you’re tempted by those upgrades, I’d stick with the Home for its larger seed capacity and two solar panels. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: The Nook is pitched as better for balconies and small spaces, whereas the Home is better for bigger yards. And I get that. The Nook is smaller, with a smaller perch and a smaller seed tray than the Home. But in my few days with it in my big backyard, the Nook’s better value beats out the Home’s convenience upgrades. Also — and this could be its killer feature — the Nook fully foiled my squirrels. Its smaller seed tray and perch seem to make it harder for them to balance (even harder if you don’t add the extended perch). I have a video where you can hear them trying to clamber onto it and giving up, whereas they got down to dinner in the Home with its deeper seed tray. (However, your squirrel mileage may vary!) Birdbuddy had a strange rollout for the Home (originally called Birdbuddy 2), releasing it to existing customers through its app a few months ago in what felt like a beta test. It seems there were a lot of kinks to work out. When I installed the Home earlier this year, I initially had trouble with Wi-Fi connectivity and battery life. But firmware updates seem to have fixed most of it. This summer, after one update, the Home’s battery lasted around three months; I only had to recharge it after a period of overcast days. [Image: The Home (blue) holds almost twice as much seed as the Nook (green) and uses two solar panels to keep the battery charged. I had no Wi-Fi connectivity issues with the Nook, and both models paired to the app much faster than the Pro. I’ve only had the Nook for a few days, so it’s too early to judge battery life. However, recharging both devices is more involved than with the Pro because you have to remove the entire camera housing, which sits inside the bird seed compartment. It’s easier to just remove the whole feeder and take it inside. The good news is that the Home is much easier to refill with birdseed without spilling it everywhere than the Pro is, thanks to a wider mouth and larger reservoir. The Nook is even easier, since you take the entire roof off to add seed — though, again, this requires removing it from its perch. You can pole-mount or hang both devices using the included hardware. One problem I have noticed with the new designs is that the roof on both no longer fully covers the seed tray, as it does with the Pro. This lets in more light for the camera, but it also means the seed gets wetter when it rains. [Image: [Image: If you are looking for your first smart bird feeder, or for a great holiday gift for your nature-loving friend or family member, the Nook is an easy buy. Upgrade to the Home if you really don’t like refilling seed and recharging batteries. If you want to add solar to the Nook, buy that up front — you can’t currently purchase the solar roof as an accessory. If you’re an existing Birdbuddy user, there are two reasons to upgrade from the Pro. First, if you’re having any issues with missed videos or slow livestream loading. Both new models load faster and capture video more reliably. Second, battery life. I had to charge the Pro every couple of weeks, even with solar. The Home got three months. Today, I wouldn’t recommend buying a Pro, even if you can find one. While I prefer its portrait camera angle and it has slightly better video quality, the connectivity and battery life of the new models are worth those compromises. I’d rather see more birds more often than a bit more of a bird less often. Birdbuddy Home ($219), Nook ($99), and Nook Solar ($159) are available now at mybirdbuddy.com and ship next month. The Nook Solar and Nook Extended Edition ($199) will be available at Target, Best Buy, and Walmart later this month. Photos, video, and screenshots by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

articles.body:
DevGAMM Awards has revealed the 70 nominated games for its third annual show, and not only do they come from 25 different countries, but more than half of the nominated titles were developed by teams of five or fewer.

The winners will be announced at a ceremony in Lisbon, Portugal, on November 18 at 10am PT/1pm ET/6pm GMT, and IGN will serve as the official streaming partner. articles.title: Mass Effect 5 Trailer Reportedly Ready to Go Before BioWare Closure
articles.summary: A Mass Effect 5 trailer was reportedly ready to go before EA canceled the game and shut BioWare down.
articles.body:
A Mass Effect 5 trailer was reportedly ready to go before EA canceled the game and shut BioWare down .

This was mentioned in a post on the subreddit for Austin , Texas, where BioWare had a studio. An alleged EA worker said “a trailer ready for Mass Effect 5 that I saw a few months ago, so I’m puzzled as to how ‘early’ they were.” IGN understands there was indeed a Mass Effect 5 trailer ready for release.

This is in reference to EA’s solitary paragraph on BioWare’s closure and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 in the memo Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, sent to staff on Wednesday:

“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.”

The mention of the next Mass Effect being in “early development” has shocked some fans, given the game was announced at The Game Awards in December 2020. At the time, BioWare said the project was in “early production.” Six years later, Mass Effect is no more.

According to Bloomberg , BioWare had around 50 staff working on Mass Effect 5 when EA closed the studio, which comes after 2024’s launch of Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA’s sales expectations. 400 jobs will reportedly go in total across EA, amounting to 3% of total staff.

BioWare’s Austin studio reportedly remains open, working to support various EA games in development. IGN has asked EA for comment.

The end of Mass Effect and BioWare comes just weeks before the annual N7 Day, set for November 7. Less than 12 months ago, Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the next Mass Effect game was still in development, to express excitement about the Amazon TV series ( which IGN understands is currently still in the works ), and to insist EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."

Fans had hoped to see more of Mass Effect 5 on N7 Day next month, but it now seems likely to pass without fanfare. “You made me laugh. Thank you,” Gamble replied to one X / Twitter user who wondered what might be announced on N7 Day next month.

Since yesterday’s dramatic news, a number of people who had worked on Mass Effect 5 talked in vague terms about the game it was shaping up to be . On X / Twitter, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a user who said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” with: “We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying.”

One person who was laid off from BioWare, cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal, took to LinkedIn to say Mass Effect 5 would have been “something special,” with “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match.”

“We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy,” he continued.

“I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special. Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career.”

We have much more on the dramatic news of BioWare's closure, including reaction from fans and the video game industry , IGN's Ryan McCaffrey on why BioWare was the greatest RPG developer ever , and Jacqueline Thomas on the sad loss of Mass Effect 5 .

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: First GTA 6 TV Commercial Strips Out Steamy Shower Scenes, but Shows More of Lucia's Fancy Hair Tech
articles.summary: GTA 6 has its first TV commercial, and it's a little different than the launch trailer.
articles.body:
GTA 6 has its first TV commercial, and it's a little different than the launch trailer.

The 90-second GTA 6 advert, which was spotted on NBC Sports, is for the most part the launch trailer Rockstar Games released last week, but the shower smooching scenes have been taken out. All three of them. Luckily, that means some of the other scenes are slightly extended, giving us a few milliseconds of extra footage.

GTA 6 – TV Spot Version 2 (90 Seconds) (Featuring Some Longer Scenes) — mnm345 (@mnm345x) October 21, 2026

GTA 6 – TV Spot Version 2 (90 Seconds) (Featuring Some Longer Scenes)

The first GTA 6 commercial aired on NBC Sports, featuring the launch trailer but with some changes: - Cut shower shots, resulting in other shots being a bit longer - Longer plane shot - Longer Jason and Lucia shot - Xbox logo completely removed due to the deal with PlayStation — GTA 6 Countdown ⏳ (@GTAVI_Countdown) October 21, 2026

The first GTA 6 commercial aired on NBC Sports, featuring the launch trailer but with some changes: - Cut shower shots, resulting in other shots being a bit longer - Longer plane shot - Longer Jason and Lucia shot - Xbox logo completely removed due to the deal with PlayStation

The slightly stretched launch trailer scenes give us a longer plane shot and a marginally extended shot of Jason and Lucia playing around while leaning on a car — now she almost falls over when Jason nudges her. And look at that hair tech!

Meanwhile, the TV spot doesn't mention Xbox as a playable platform for GTA 6 at all, despite GTA 6 launching on PS5 and both Xbox Series consoles next month. This is further evidence of the extensive partnership between Sony and Rockstar for GTA 6 marketing rights, which has seen official trailers and the extended gameplay look feature gameplay captured from PS5, and messaging that calls PS5 “the best place to play.”

More casual fans who might discover that GTA 6 is coming out at all from an advert on something like live sports might reasonably conclude that PlayStation is the only place to play Rockstar’s open world crime sequel, which is no doubt what Sony's hoping for from its partnership.

Last month, Microsoft stepped in to address a report that claimed GTA 6 preorders were “heavily skewed” toward PS5 over Xbox Series X and S. In a report about recent layoffs and studio reorganization at Xbox , The Verge’s Tom Warren said the PS5’s dominance over GTA 6 preorders was “ringing yet more alarm bells" about Xbox as a platform.

However, Xbox CSO Matthew Ball insisted that Microsoft was “very happy” with GTA 6 preorders, and that its internal data showed preorders were matching “our share of the console market.” Sony has published blog posts talking about the features of the PS5 that GTA 6 will use, such as the speaker in the DualSense controller and the pad's haptic feedback. Other additions to GTA 6's PS5 marketing campaign include a version of the PlayStation app logo on smartphones that features GTA 6 colors and pale tree fronds. So, with PlayStation’s partnership in full swing, preorders being “heavily skewed” toward PS5 doesn't come as much of a surprise.

Miami is currently completely taken over by the game, which is set in a fictionalized Miami called Vice City, as well as the surrounding area. articles.title: Gran Turismo Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controller Is Up for Preorder in Celebration of the Series 30th Anniversary
articles.body:
Heads up, racing fans. We’re coming up on 30 years since the original Gran Turismo game launched on PS1. To celebrate, Sony is releasing a new Gran Turismo limited-edition DualSense PS5 controller. It’s up for preorder now ( see it at Amazon ). It costs $84.99 and is set to release on December 10.

Gran Turismo Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controller

Sony says this controller “pays tribute to The Real Driving Simulator,” a nickname for the long-running video game series from Polyphony Digital and Kazunori Yamauchi. It’s certainly a sleek-looking design. It features a textured, carbon-fiber-style front plate that looks super high quality and gives it a sheen of elegance.

Although the controller’s trailer features prominent red and blue stripes, the actual controller is more chromatically subdued. It does have two racing stripes spanning the Touch Pad vertically, but they’re black. The face buttons are gray-on-black, as are the tiny arrows on the D-pad.

The controller does have just a touch of color in the two rectangles above the Gran Turismo branding below the D-pad, and on a pair of symbols on the Touch Pad. Other racing imagery can be found on the grips as well, including a circled “30,” no doubt in reference to the anniversary.

Aside from the design, it’s a standard PS5 DualSense controller, capable of all the same things the controller can do. It has adaptive triggers with force feedback, haptic feedback, a built-in microphone and headset jack, and more. It’s compatible with PS5 of course, but also with PC, Mac, and mobile devices.

Kazunori Yamauchi, aka “Kaz,” the CEO of Polyphony Digital Inc., wrote about the controller, “Thirty years ago, Gran Turismo began with a vision to share the beauty and joy of the automobile. This commemorative controller celebrates the journey we have shared together, and I am deeply grateful to everyone whose passion continues to inspire us.”

This isn’t the only fancy new PS5 controller design that’s currently available for preorder. You can also pick up a Grand Theft Auto 6 limited-edition PS5 DualSense controller , coming out on November 19 alongside the game. And you can see every color of PS5 DualSense controller available as well.

articles.title: Skate Studio Also Hit With Cuts as Scope of EA's Mass Layoffs Becomes Clearer
articles.summary: Following the announcement that EA is closing down Mass Effect developer BioWare, staff at the studio behind the latest Skate game have also reported suffering layoffs.
articles.body:
Following the announcement that EA is closing down Mass Effect developer BioWare, staff at the studio behind the latest Skate game have also reported suffering layoffs.

The live-service skating game was briefly mentioned as an ongoing active project in the memo EA sent to staff about the dramatic cuts, but an undetermined number of Skate developers said they had been let go from the studio behind it, Full Circle.

Seasonal creative director, John Epler, wrote on LinkedIn (via VGC ): “Well, as of today, my role at Full Circle has been eliminated. Coming up on my 19 year anniversary in the industry — and all of that time spent at EA — I can’t say I’m sad. A little nervous, definitely, but I’m looking forward to doing something new.”

Senior game designer Adam Martinazzi also confirmed his departure. “I, like many of the other talented people at Full Circle, was let go today,” he said. “Part of me is sad and frustrated. The other part accepts that this is a ‘just part of the industry.' And the other other part is grateful for the time I got to spend working on a cool game with lots of awesome people.”

Another senior designer, David Milne, was among those affected. “Looks like my position at Full Circle has been eliminated. Sad to have to leave. I really enjoyed working on Skate and loved the team I worked with. But it’s on to the next thing now.”

Full Circle was previously hit by a wave of layoffs back in February. “The teammates affected are talented colleagues and friends who helped build the foundation of Skate,” Full Circle said at the time. “Their creativity and dedication are deeply ingrained in what players experience today. This decision is not a reflection of their impact and we’re committed to supporting them through this transition.”

EA's memo to staff had this to say about Skate:

"For skate., we’ve had a lot of success in bringing players into the game, and we need to create an experience that keeps them engaged over the long-term. To do that, we are making changes to the studio to have a more focused, smaller team to deliver on a very clear roadmap for our community that we believe will build a healthier and more sustainable business."

According to Bloomberg , 400 jobs are going across EA, amounting to 3% of total staff. 50 of these were working on the next Mass Effect before BioWare's closure. Just two weeks ago, Full Circle published a statement addressing mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate . This platform allows fans to play the game offline, create private servers, make their own maps, and more. Full Circle acknowledged the importance of community mods, but stood firm against those that bypass paid cosmetics or make money off of new features.

Full Circle went on to confirm that it was aware that players want “more freedom and custom features,” and revealed that it was building “official, secure access tools that enable broader, deeper community creation.”

EA went private earlier this year with Saudi Arabian involvement . "This moment recognizes the extraordinary people whose creativity, ambition and passion have made EA one of the world's leading interactive entertainment companies," CEO Andrew Wilson, who pocketed a compensation package of $38.6 million for the 2026 fiscal year, said at the time. Wilson had Battlefield 6 to thank for strong performance for the fiscal year, but a record-breaking launch didn’t stop EA from laying off staff across Battlefield Studios .

articles.title: 'Jaws Hit the Floor' at Auction House as Retired Decorator Sells Pokémon Cards for $2 Million
articles.summary: A retired decorator from the UK just became a millionaire by selling a bunch of Pokémon cards collecting dust in his loft for $2 million.
articles.body:
A retired decorator from the UK just became a millionaire by selling a bunch of Pokémon cards collecting dust in his loft for $2 million.

The man, from Woking, UK, said he had no idea the cards were valuable until he read about a single card fetching £6,000 (approx. $8,000).

The cards were auctioned off at Surrey-based auction house Ewbank's on Wednesday for £1.56 million (approx. $2 million). "I know people always talk about finding treasure in the attic, but in my case that is literally true," said the anonymous retiree, via the BBC .

"When my son was young, in the late 1990s, he started getting cards and swapping them at school. I thought they looked nice and wondered whether they might be a good investment. He had his own cards, but he never got to touch these, I'm glad to say."

8 Stunning Cards in Pokémon TCG: Scarlet & Violet Shrouded Fable

He stored the cards away after his son lost interest in collecting them all. One set, which the newly minted millionaire bought from a Malaysian eBay seller for £300 (approx. $400), went for a whopping £75,000 (approx. $100,000) at auction.

An auction official said "jaws hit the floor" when the man showed them his collection. "When we saw what he had — all in mint condition — we couldn't believe it," said head of trading cards at Ewbank’s, James Spooner.

It was the most successful sale Ewbank’s has seen in over 30 years of business. The Legendary Collection Complete Master Set alone went for £100,000 (approx. $133,000).

Ewbank conducted the sale himself. When it went through, he told bidders he was "going for a lie down.” There was global buzz for the auction leading up to the day, and bidders phoned in from all over the world. Interest was particularly high because the entire collection was pristine, complete, and untouched — stuffed with every rarity of card you could imagine.

In April this year, teacher Andrew Braund approached Ewbank’s with a 20-year-old collection of Pokémon cards he had kept in his parents’ attic. He consigned the three rarest cards to Ewbank’s who took £32,800 for them on April 16, with Andrew using the proceeds to pay for his August wedding .

These cards have some way to go before coming close to the most expensive Pokémon card ever sold, however. In February, the Pikachu Illustrator card sold for an eye-watering $16,492,000 after 41 days of bidding. It belonged to American influencer and wrestler Logan Paul, who bought it for $5.275 million in July 2021.

More than 10 billion Pokémon cards were printed last year alone, and 85 billion have been created in total. That volume makes it hard to come across complete sets and the rarest cards, which are so sought after that people pull off Pokémon card heists to steal them.

articles.title: EA Never Knew What It Had With BioWare, and It’s All of Our Loss
articles.summary: EA's complete misunderstanding of BioWare's RPG heritage and a desire for mass market, microtransaction-fuelled action games has robbed us of one of the industry's greats.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Matt Purslow, who has played BioWare's RPGs for almost his entire life. "My hotel's as clean as an elven arse!" remains one of his favourite NPC voice lines almost 30 years later.

In 2012 and 2013, EA was named the “Worst Company in America” in public polls held by Consumerist, beating out the likes of big oil, big pharma, and any other big corpo you can think of. During those years, the mega-publisher released Dead Space 3, Crysis 3, and Mass Effect 3. Each of this trio of three-quels is in some way responsible for the company’s reputation at the time. Crysis was considered a rote follow-up, Dead Space’s microtransactions were seen as greedy, and disappointment over the finale of Mass Effect’s trilogy-concluding chapter provoked more outrage than many political scandals.

The idea that the early 2010s could be considered some of EA’s better years, then, should be absurd. But here we are . The colossal company’s latest 400 layoffs follow three subsequent years of severe cuts, including last year’s 300 staff , the cancellation of a Titanfall game, and the shuttering of Cliffhanger Games and its Black Panther project . In the surviving projects we can see just what EA values: annualised sports games with huge microtransaction revenue and live-service shooters with huge microtransaction revenue.

Video games at triple-A scale are, of course, a business. An industry. A means to make profit. Its role as a financial machine is why EA is now owned by a group of investors including Saudi Arabia's PIF and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners . But it's never felt more obvious that the suits who just deleted BioWare from a spreadsheet don’t care about the ‘arts’ in Electronic Arts. How far the company has fallen since 1983, when it asked “Can a computer make you cry?” in an advertisement promoting its creative ambition .

The more cynical parts of the internet see BioWare’s shuttering as something of a mercy, a failing studio put out to pasture. The putting down of a sick dog. And it’s true that the studio’s best days were seemingly behind it – its three most recent projects, Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard, were all disappointments to varying degrees. But while those most cynical voices accuse those within BioWare of betraying the studio’s roots, I think the issues lie squarely with EA. As IGN contributor Jeremy Peel wrote on social media yesterday, “I’ve chatted to enough veterans to know that BioWare succeeded despite EA’s ownership, not because of it. The studio steered a ship with a saboteur in the engine room.”

That’s not to say BioWare hasn’t made mistakes of its own. During an interview with IGN earlier this year, veteran Dragon Age executive producer Mark Darrah explained that Anthem was pitched internally as ‘the future of storytelling’ by Casey Hudson, the celebrated director of the Mass Effect trilogy and BioWare’s general manager through much of Anthem’s development. He remembers the mechsuit shooter being conceived as “What if we said it’s still BioWare, but it’s completely not BioWare?”

But is that attitude born of wanting to disintegrate years of RPG pedigree, or an attempt to secure survival within a ruthless publisher whose primary motivator is extraordinary money, not sustainable art?

“They wanted every franchise to be a billion-dollar franchise”, Darrah said, noting EA’s internal goals for every franchise were to hit a minimum 40% profit margin, and for that to equate to $50 million in total profit. Even in its prime, BioWare wasn’t well positioned to achieve that. RPGs, particularly the grand, cinematic ones that made up BioWare’s most beloved era, are not cheap to produce. And, compared to the mass popularity of EA Sports’ annualised output, they’re quite niche.

Since it was acquired by EA in 2007, BioWare was constantly at the mercy of a parent company that had no interest in (and probably zero understanding of) role-playing games. You can see the battle in each successive game post-Mass Effect, with the crunchy RPG systems of Baldur’s Gate and Neverwinter Nights stripped out in favour of more action, more linearity, more streamlined cinematic gloss. And, for a short while, that battle between EA’s demand for mass market products and BioWare’s desire to build first-class RPGs resulted in something special. Mass Effect 2 is one of the greatest games ever made because it balances blockbuster action with the deep character development and meaningful choices of the best D&D session.

But post Dragon Age: Inquisition, things began to fall apart. The disasters of Anthem and The Veilguard are well documented to be rooted in the difficult relationship between a single-player RPG studio and its Ultimate Team revenue-obsessed parent. And so after all it went through , it’s a miracle that The Veilguard even exists. But its fate as a bitter disappointment was, sadly, practically assured from the moment it began its troubled journey.

If BioWare was an isolated incident, it could be chalked up to EA mismanaging a studio that specialised in games it simply didn’t understand. But BioWare is only the latest in a long, long line of casualties. We can rewind as far back as the 1990s and find studios that it acquired, muddled, and eventually shuttered. Origin Systems. Bullfrog Productions. Kesmai. When EA acquired BioWare in 2007, it took on Pandemic Studios at the same time – the creators of the iconic Star Wars: Battlefront and destructive Mercenaries. Two years later it was gone.

But closure is simply one of the ugly fates that EA bestows on those it chews up. Over time, many studios are rebranded, reshuffled, and ingested into the big machine. Medal of Honor creator DreamWorks Interactive became part of EA in 2000 and within a few years it had been merged with what was left of Command & Conquer creator Westwood Studios (itself bought in 1998, closed in 2003). Renamed EA Los Angeles, the developer was put to work on Lord of the Rings and C&C strategy games, before then being re-badged as Danger Close and tasked with rebooting Medal of Honor to compete with Call of Duty’s Modern Warfare – an impossible task that sealed its miserable fate.

That reduction of studios to simple labour continues. Just this year we’ve seen Criterion, the racing games specialist EA bought in 2004, transformed into “A Battlefield Studio” – destined to work alongside three other studios on a multiplayer shooter franchise that’s a million miles away from its Burnout and Need for Speed roots. Only the very lucky (or very profitable) get to be ingested by EA and retain their personality, it seems.

I recently saw a Reddit thread that emphasised the importance of treating game developers like music bands rather than software companies. The OP suggested that, like a band, the original creatives are the studio and any change in staff or leadership equals the effective end of it. That’s perhaps a little too strict a definition for me personally, but I believe there’s more to that concept than individual people – like a band, a studio is a mantra. A creative philosophy. An artistic dream. Beneath all the HR paperwork and budget spreadsheets, studios have soul and purpose. That’s something that can be shared among new hires, passed down through generations, but it’s something that needs to be preserved. A studio is much, much more than a group of bodies to be thrown at whatever project is in need of staffing, to develop according to whatever trend is profitable, and that should be respected.

Sadly, that is not how the gears of private equity-financed corporations spin. And so just as BioWare wasn’t the first, I don’t expect it to be the last. As part of its plans for its next chapter , EA explained that while Motive’s Iron Man game and the third Star Wars Jedi are still in development, "beyond that, we will concentrate our efforts on fewer simultaneous, large-scale projects." That sure sounds like EA’s interest in action-adventure games is dwindling, at least as far as internal development goes (its publishing of Hazelight’s co-op adventures, It Takes Two and Split Fiction, has proven commercially and critically successful, and so that kind of thing may continue). Respawn is already confirmed to be collaborating with DICE on a “future project” , so it feels only a matter of time until all of EA’s shooter studios are combined to become a homogeneous whole. And with that consolidation, EA will have finally streamlined into a company focused on annualised sports games with huge microtransaction revenue and live-service shooters with huge microtransaction revenue.

“Can a computer make you cry?” the company asked in 1983. Yes, but not in the way that advert intended.

Matt Purslow is IGN's Executive Editor of Features.

articles.title: Star Wars: The Old Republic Lead Writer Mourns Death of BioWare as Farewell Post Leaves Out MMO
articles.summary: The lead writer of Star Wars: The Old Republic has expressed sadness at the death of former developer BioWare, after the studio's official farewell statement failed to mention the MMO.
articles.body:
The lead writer of Star Wars: The Old Republic has expressed sadness at the death of former developer BioWare, after the studio's official farewell statement failed to mention the MMO.

BioWare's statement on its closure namechecked Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem, but Star Wars: The Old Republic was conspicuous by its absence.

Star Wars: The Old Republic , or SWTOR, was developed by BioWare and released all the way back in 2011, and the studio ran the game until it was handed over to Broadsword in 2023. But in the 12 years that BioWare did run the game, it ended up with more writing and voice work than any other BioWare game in history.

In a social media post , SWTOR lead writer Caitlin Sullivan Kelly called the situation "heartbreaking," adding: "No mention of the game that's been going for almost fifteen years, that supported the studio and all of its projects with income and manpower and time (sometimes to our own detriment)."

Indeed SWTOR carried on for years, generating revenue and maintaining a steady playerbase throughout its existence, even if it wasn't quite as large as titans of the MMO world like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV. But, BioWare did pull members of the SWTOR team away from the MMO to support projects like Anthem, according to Kotaku , which ended up failing almost immediately. Yet SWTOR lived on, and continues to do so.

There could be any number of reasons why SWTOR was left out of BioWare's statement. Maybe there were legal issues given it no longer operates the game, for example. "I said this when we got moved to Broadsword, DA:O was the game that made me want to be a game dev. I started playing SWTOR BECAUSE it was a BioWare game," Kelly continued. "I can’t help but feel sad that the studio a lot of us loved even before we worked there leaves us out of the history books."

articles.title: Final James Bond Screen Tests Are Underway With Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Others on the Shortlist
articles.summary: Reports suggest that the final James Bond screen tests are underway, with actors like Jack Lowden and Callum Turner on the shortlist.
articles.body:
Reports suggest that the final James Bond screen tests are underway, with actors like Jack Lowden and Callum Turner on the shortlist.

As reported by both Deadline and The Hollywood Reporter , final screen tests for the next Bond are expected to take place this week. As it stands, there's only a small handful of actors still in the running to become 007. Jack Lowden and Callum Turner have both been corroborated by the two outlets, but Deadline also noted that Josh O'Connor is also in the mix.

A fourth actor is also rumored to be in the mix, though it's unclear who. The Hollywood Reporter ruled out Jack O'Connell as the fourth mystery actor. Both Deadline and THR noted that Jacob Elordi is not testing for the role, despite having previously been rumored . The actors who are up for the part are expected to be tested on stunts, dialogue, and camera presence.

The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007

As a result, we can likely expect the next Bond to be announced sometime in November or December. The film will be director Denis Villeneuve's next project following the release of Dune Part 3, though it currently has no release date. Though, if production begins next year, it could release in late 2028. The film already has a script, so it's just a matter of assembling all of the pieces.

Casting for the next Bond has been underway since spring , and there has been no shortage of rumors about who will don the tux. Although Jack Lowden appears to be a favorite among fans, ex-Bond actor Daniel Craig told IGN last year that he was rooting for Josh O'Connor and joked that he started a rumor that he was up for the part. Now, it seems that joke has actually become reality, with O'Connor as a finalist.

We also have no idea what the new direction will be for James Bond. The Daniel Craig films were more grounded and serious, something that would likely lend itself to Denis Villeneuve's style. It seems unlikely we'll get another origin story since Casino Royale did that so tactfully, and 007 First Light also successfully put its own spin on things earlier this year. Early reports suggested that producers were eyeing a younger Bond, but all three of the named candidates are 36 years old, just two years younger than Craig was in Casino Royale. It's possible the direction has changed, but it may come at the cost of longevity.

Craig was injured many times during his tenure as James Bond , and the stunts became more difficult as he got older . Maybe the producers don't intend on having the next Bond play the role for 15 years like Craig, though.

articles.body:
Yesterday, at the end of a stream on YouTube , the electronic music duo Daft Punk teased a collaboration with LEGO. Today LEGO confirmed it. A LEGO Daft Punk set is indeed coming soon. The set is based on the stage setup for Daft Punk’s 2007 Alive tour.

Confirmed in a LEGO Ideas blog post , the set sprang from a LEGO Ideas submission from creator RobotRock , which has been sitting in the “Parking Lot” for several years. According to the blog post, “The Parking Lot is where selected Product Ideas get extra review time before a final decision is made.”

LEGO Ideas is a program in which LEGO fans and builders can create their own sets and submit them for consideration to become actual released products. Once a LEGO Ideas submission is approved, the creators of the set work with official LEGO designers to make any changes necessary to turn it into an officially released set.

That’s the step this upcoming LEGO Daft Punk set is currently in. No release date or pricing information is available yet, but we expect to hear more soon.

In a related press release , LEGO also announced a broader LEGO/Daft Punk partnership that hints at more crossovers besides this one set. The partnership even has a video to announce the musicians' entry into the LEGO universe.

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 Dev Says BioWare Saw What Larian and CD Projekt Had Done in the RPG Space and Was Taking the Franchise to ‘The Next Level’
articles.summary: A former Mass Effect 5 developer has said that BioWare had seen what RPG powerhouses Larian and CD Projekt were achieving with their games, and was responding by taking Mass Effect to “the next level.”
articles.body:
A former Mass Effect 5 developer has said that BioWare had seen what RPG powerhouses Larian and CD Projekt were achieving with their games, and was responding by taking Mass Effect to “the next level.”

Yesterday, EA sent shockwaves through the industry with the announcement that the next Mass Effect game was canceled and its developer, BioWare, was shutting down . Around 50 people were reportedly working on the game before development ended.

Since yesterday’s dramatic news, a number of people who had worked on Mass Effect 5 talked in vague terms about the game it was shaping up to be . On X / Twitter, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a user who said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” with: “We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying.”

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

One person who was laid off from BioWare, cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal, took to LinkedIn to say Mass Effect 5 would have been “something special,” offering players “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match.”

“We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy,” he continued.

“I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special. Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career.”

Both Larian and CD Projekt have enjoyed enormous success with their RPGs over the last decade, while BioWare struggled with a series of disappointing releases that failed to meet EA’s expectations. After the franchise-best sales of Dragon Age: Inquisition, BioWare sought live-service success with Anthem, then spent the best part of a decade on the troubled Dragon Age: The Veilguard. Both underperformed. Mass Effect, meanwhile, has seen mixed success. Mass Effect Andromeda is widely considered a disappointment among fans, though the series' more recent Legendary Edition remaster was well-received.

BioWare had spent the past half a decade teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story. We'd had it confirmed that Mass Effect 5 would have been set hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3 , and feature a narrative that re-centers the action on the franchise's original Milky Way setting, long after the Reapers were defeated.

Meanwhile, CD Projekt has released The Witcher 3, which is considered by some to be the greatest fantasy RPG of all time, Cyberpunk 2077, which after a disastrous launch is now considered one of the best sci-fi RPGs ever made, and is set to follow both up with various sequels that are among the most-anticipated video games on earth.

Larian saw critical and commercial acclaim with its Divinity: Original Sin games, but 2023’s Baldur’s Gate 3 propelled the studio into the stratosphere, selling millions of copies and resetting expectations around what a role-playing game could be.

It’s hard to say what Mass Effect 5 might have been, but based on comments from former developers, it was being made with the likes of The Witcher 3, Cyberpunk, and Baldur’s Gate 3 in mind. The line about “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match,” is quite the claim, but to me is clearly in reaction to the likes of Baldur’s Gate 3, which reacts to player choice and experimentation in a way that goes above and beyond most games ever released.

articles.title: Mike Mignola Resurrects the Hellboy Universe for B.P.R.D.: Declassified
articles.summary: We've got an exclusive first look at BPRD: Declassified, the latest addition to Mike Mignola's long-running Hellboy universe.
articles.body:
Even the end of the world can't keep the Hellboy franchise down. Creator Mike Mignola is once again revisiting his most iconic horror universe for a new miniseries called B.P.R.D.: Declassified.

IGN can exclusively reveal the cover art and first details for B.P.R.D.: Declassified #1, which releases in February 2027. See artist Mike Norton's cover art below:

B.P.R.D.: Declassified is cowritten by Mignola and Chris Roberson (iZombie), with art by Norton (Battlepug) and colors by Hellboy mainstay Dave Stewart. The first issue also features a variant cover by Gabriel Hardman (Green Lantern: Earth One).

Here's the official summary of the new series:

Fans last saw the psychic B.P.R.D. agent Susan Xiang in 2025’s The Shadow of the Golden Crane by Chris Roberson and Michael Avon Oeming, where she investigated her family’s connection to the mysterious Golden Crane Society. Now, she’s teaming up with astral projecting B.P.R.D agent Victor Koestler for an otherworldly missing person investigation.

Henry Rouch was overseas working on a classified government project before he mysteriously vanished. The supernatural circumstances surrounding his disappearance means the B.P.R.D. has been called in to investigate, but the agents soon discover that there’s much more to this case than meets the eye.

"We’ve been teasing around the edges of a larger story involving an occult cold war in the pages of Hellboy and the B.P.R.D. and elsewhere for a while now, usually in the background of another supernatural investigation or monster hunt of some kind,” said Roberson in a press release. “B.P.R.D.: Declassified is a chance to pull the curtain back a bit and focus our full attention on what’s been going on in the shadows, and to see that the agents of the B.P.R.D. aren’t the only players on the board. The stakes are higher than Susan Xiang and company ever suspected."

articles.title: 3 Very Different Survival Games from indie.io Featured in Steam Next Fest
articles.body:
October is the perfect time to dive into a survival game, and there are three from publishing platform indie.io that are part of Steam Next Fest from now until October 26. And these three prove that “survival game” can mean very different things and have completely different gameplay.

One is a co-op horror-comedy set in a coal mine, one is an open-world sandbox after a zombie apocalypse, and one sees you stranded alone on a 24-island archipelago after your ship mysteriously crashes. You can play all three games right now, with two of them having free demos as part of Steam Next Fest and one already fully released with a huge new content update for spooky season.

Three generations ago, the sky froze. Now, your coal mining town is perpetually covered in snow. You might think that would be the end of the mine, but nope, the state kept it open and is forcing miners to continue delving into its depths. That might sound a bit dystopian, but it’s a premise that Coal Duty mines for humor as well as coal.

It’s a co-op extraction game for between 1–5 players, and you play as a group of miners who must navigate the many dangers of the mine to survive and get out with the materials you gathered. Each run is procedurally generally, so you’ll need to work together with your teammates to figure out how to progress.

That teamwork relies on one of Coal Duty’s most interesting mechanics: proximity voice chat. You can talk to each other, but your teammates will only hear you if they’re close by. You can call out to let them know you found the correct route, warn them of dangers, or anything else you think is worth mentioning. But be wary: Everything else in the mine can also hear you if they’re close enough, and you don’t want to activate any dangers because you got chatty.

Those dangers are plentiful and varied. There are dozens of different creatures, each of which have characteristics you’ll need to figure out to learn how to effectively deal with them. Some are blind, some are fast, some will disguise themselves as coal. Nothing beats hearing your friend suddenly panic because an enemy startled them, only to attract more unwanted attention with their shrieking.

A free demo of Coal Duty is playable now during Steam Next Fest, and it’s a great time for you and your friends to give it a try. It releases in Early Access on October 27, the day after Next Fest ends. The demo is a deliberate slice of the game, while the Early Access release will add more mine floors, creatures, and an escape machine.

IGN covered HumanitZ’s 1.0 launch in February, and this isometric open-world zombie survival sandbox game just dropped its biggest update since on October 19. It introduced some major new additions: NPC recruitment, player zombification, a Halloween event, a headshot-only mode, new gear, and more.

Once you finish the Radio Tower quest, you’re now able to recruit NPC survivors you meet in the world. They can follow you on runs, work your base, stand guard, or be sent on tasks. You can build two extra outposts and send your recruits between them depending on your needs, and each NPC has their own traits.

You need to actually keep an eye on those traits, too. Some only become clear after an NPC has been in your community for a while, and they might reveal they’re not as friendly as you thought they were. The NPC recruitment feature is available in single-player and hosted multiplayer modes, since games on servers have other players to fill this role.

With the update, if you die to a zeek (HumanitZ’s name for zombies) or the infection, your character will rise as a zeek themselves. The zeek version of you will wander the world with all your loot, but you can track them down to kill them and get that loot back.

The Halloween update added themed cosmetics, quests, weapons, and world props. The headshot-only mode is what it sounds like: zeeks will only die if you shoot them in the head, which ramps up the difficulty level. The update’s new gear includes a lever-action rifle, nail gun, ponchos, balaclavas, and lootable large toolboxes.

If you’ve played HumanitZ before, the update is significant enough it warrants coming back for another playthrough. If you haven’t, this is your invitation to give it a go. It’s currently sitting at a Mostly Positive rating on Steam with more than 4,400 reviews.

IGN first covered Mayday: The Survival Island when its demo came to gamescom and PAX West in August and early September. In the time since, that demo has undergone significant changes but is still free to try out on Steam.

The updated demo includes extensive bug fixes and polish, bringing it in line with what gameplay will look like in the full release. It also expanded the house building system and introduced a substantial chunk of new content. Your save data in the demo can be carried over to the full release when it comes out on November 2, so it’s essentially like getting a head start.

The basic premise of the game is that your ship crashes and you wash ashore on a mysterious island, which you discover is one of 24 making up a massive archipelago. Each island is hand-crafted by the small dev team at Pequi Studios, they’re not procedurally generated. They all have different environments, materials to gather, and treasures to find.

You’ll need to use those materials to create tools, which can then be used to hunt, fish, grow crops, and ultimately build a homestead for yourself. Basically, everything you need to do to survive. You can take however much time you want building up your base on each island, and when you move on to the next one is up to you. As you progress, you’ll uncover secrets about the archipelago, what brought you here, and find out if it’s even possible to get back home.

articles.title: Dispatch Gets Over 16 Hours of New Content With Commentary Track, Mobile Version, and Live Concert to Celebrate Its First Anniversary
articles.summary: Dispatch is now officially one year old! To celebrate, Adhoc is giving fans oodles of new content in the form of a commentary track and storyboard modes, a new mobile version of the game, a live concert with a performance from Prism herself, and yes, more merch.
articles.body:
Dispatch is now officially one year old! To celebrate, AdHoc Studio is giving fans oodles of new content in the form of a commentary track and storyboard modes, a new mobile version of the game, a live concert with a performance from Prism herself, and yes, more merch.

AdHoc’s debut title, Dispatch , released to rave reviews on October 22, 2025. Made up of Telltale alumni, the devs truly flexed their storytelling chops with this game, bringing players along for Robert’s journey from zero to hero alongside a chaotic cast of lovable, super-powered characters.

A year later, fans are anxiously awaiting more updates on AdHoc’s next project — but in the meantime, they can whet their appetites on some exciting additions to Dispatch and fun experiences that bring the game's digital world to reality.

Now included in Dispatch's Deluxe Edition are a Commentary Mode and Storyboard Mode. Commentary Mode brings players back to the days of DVD Special Features with two separate audio tracks, where the game’s actors and developers chat about the project in the background as the game progresses. Each choice will give you new insights into the game, so there’s even more replayability for curious fans who want all the gritty details about how Dispatch was made. Storyboard mode shows players the sketches that laid out how the game's scenes were planned, and it can even be paired with Commentary Mode for a double-whammy.

The Deluxe Edition also comes with a digital art book and four digital comics. What’s more, those who already own the Deluxe Edition will get the Commentary and Storyboard modes for free, while those who have the standard version of the game can upgrade for $10.99 USD.

But wait, there’s more! Dispatch is also coming to mobile, letting you join Rob on his adventures wherever you’re at in the world. The game releases on Android and iOS on December 9, 2026, with additional support for Google Play Games on PC. The base game has been rebuilt for touch screens and vertical play, and mobile players can get the first four episodes for free. The full release will cost $19.99, with pre-orders opening on the Google Play store and Apple store soon.

Fans have been begging for more merchandise in the months since Dispatch first came to Steam, and now, they finally get their wish. A three-record soundtrack vinyl set, featuring artwork from Dispatch’s art director, Derek Stratton, will be available to purchase, and 100 of those will be signed by him. Shirts, hoodies, and four physical comics are also available for purchase, with each volume boasting an individual cover that creates an epic battle scene when placed side by side. A Dispatch: Design Works hardcover book and collectible box are also up for sale, going behind the scenes with concept art, cast interviews, developer insights, and more. And for the real collectors out there, the first 1,000 orders placed on the official online store will get a never-before-seen limited edition, numbered collector’s card.

Perhaps most excitingly, the music of Dispatch is getting brought to life with a special concert for one night only. On Thursday, December 3, fans can gather at the AVALON Hollywood to watch ‘Hoes Depressed’ singer and the voice of Prism, THOT SQUAD, perform songs from the game live alongside Bershy, Primer, Caroline Kingsbury, and Fartbarf. Tickets for this event are extremely limited, with AdHoc Studio email subscribers getting first pick before they open up to the general public. It's an in-person event only, so it won't be streamed, and you'll want to get your tickets fast.

"Dispatch was only possible because of folks who believed in it enough to show up and do their best work. In our industry, it's often really hard to showcase those people and how the development process actually works, but fortunately our game is very weird and specific and affords us some unique opportunities." said Nick Herman, Co-Creative Director on Dispatch and COO of AdHoc Studio.

"So for the fans who made Dispatch a part of their lives, we wanted to give them more ways to experience the world they love, whether that’s playing alongside the cast and crew, experiencing the entire game in its original storyboards, or hanging out together IRL at the wildest version of a Dispatch concert our finance team would sign off on."

If you haven't gotten to play Dispatch yet, now is the time. IGN scored the game a glowing 9 out of 10 , with reviewer Sara Thwaites calling it a "sharp-witted workplace comedy that charms with its smart dialogue choices, great writing, and lovably aggravating cast."

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 Trailer Leaks Online With 'Mass Effect: Universe' Title, Reveals Returning Characters and Much More
articles.summary: A trailer for Mass Effect 5 meant for internal purposes at BioWare has leaked online, offering a glimpse at what might have been.
articles.body:
A trailer for Mass Effect 5 meant for internal purposes at BioWare has leaked online, offering a glimpse at what might have been.

The trailer, which IGN has verified as legitimate, was created for internal purposes only and was not meant for the public. It appeared on Reddit just a day after EA's shock cancelation of the game and its developer, BioWare . It includes the title 'Mass Effect: Universe.'

The trailer begins with a message: "The following is in-engine footage from our small team. It uses our pre-production assets.”

The trailer has a number of familiar elements, including weaponry, powers, and alien species we've seen in previous Mass Effect games. There's a glimpse at a sex scene, a Mass Effect relay, space travel, and a nightclub, all Mass Effect staples. There's even a galaxy map on display inside your ship.

It looks like players would have assumed the role of a former military operative now in a "new line of work." The job is to stop fires before they start. An older Liara T'Soni appears, helping the player character out in a bar fight.

BioWare had spent the past half a decade teasing the next Mass Effect's setting and story. We'd had it confirmed that Mass Effect 5 would have been set hundreds of years after Mass Effect 3 , and feature a narrative that re-centers the action on the franchise's original Milky Way setting, long after the Reapers were defeated.

On X / Twitter, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a user who said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” with: “We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying.”

One person who was laid off from BioWare, cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal, took to LinkedIn to say Mass Effect 5 would have been “something special,” offering players “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match.”

“We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy,” he continued.

“I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking, and sad for the small, talented group of devs who were all punching above their weight to make something special. Please consider those who stayed with BioWare until the very end. They are truly some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career.”

Earlier today, IGN reported that a Mass Effect 5 trailer was ready to go before EA canceled the game and shut BioWare down. This was first mentioned in a post on the subreddit for Austin , Texas, where BioWare had a studio. An alleged EA worker spoke of “a trailer ready for Mass Effect 5 that I saw a few months ago, so I’m puzzled as to how ‘early’ they were.”

This is in reference to EA’s solitary paragraph on BioWare’s closure and the cancelation of Mass Effect 5 in the memo Cam Weber, president and chief studios officer, and David Tinson, president and COO, sent to staff on Wednesday:

“As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect. We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly.”

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

The mention of the next Mass Effect being in “early development” shocked some fans, given the game was announced at The Game Awards in December 2020. At the time, BioWare said the project was in “early production.”

According to Bloomberg , BioWare had around 50 staff working on Mass Effect 5 when EA closed the studio, which comes after 2024’s launch of Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA’s sales expectations. 400 jobs will reportedly go in total across EA, amounting to 3% of total staff.

BioWare’s Austin studio reportedly remains open, working to support various EA games in development. IGN has asked EA for comment.

The end of Mass Effect and BioWare comes just weeks before the annual N7 Day, set for November 7. Less than 12 months ago, Mike Gamble, executive producer of Mass Effect at BioWare, celebrated N7 Day to say the next Mass Effect game was still in development, to express excitement about the Amazon TV series ( which IGN understands is currently still in the works ), and to insist EA and BioWare "remain committed to telling more stories in this universe."

Fans had hoped to see more of Mass Effect 5 on N7 Day next month, but it now seems likely to pass without fanfare. “You made me laugh. Thank you,” Gamble replied to one X / Twitter user who wondered what might be announced on N7 Day next month.
