articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever Breathes New Life Into an Iconic Classic
articles.body:
World of Warcraft first launched more than 20 years ago, becoming the king of the MMORPG genre and establishing Azeroth as one of the most iconic worlds in gaming. Now, Blizzard Entertainment is reimagining that world with World of Warcraft: Forever, which launches on November 4 and builds on what made the original great while adding a ton of new content.

The feel of the OG game has been carried over to WoW: Forever, with the original character models and spell animations still intact. The level 60 cap is also back, as is the slower leveling experience that made each level up feel like an accomplishment. But the details have been enhanced, with improved core systems, items, UI, and world graphics.

The headliner additions are new zones, a new playable race, and a bunch of new quests. We’re not going to ruin the feeling of discovery by going into too much detail about the new locations, but we can share that even areas long-time players are familiar with have some new surprises. There are over 1,000 new quests, which will take you to corners of the map you’ve never visited before.

The main new zone we will call out is Zephras Isle, a starting area that’s in crisis after the air spirits that protected it vanished and its current people are divided about what to do next. This area is notable because it’s home to WoW: Forever’s brand-new playable race, the elven Skyborne.

They can be part of either the Horde or Alliance, with their racial abilities determined by their alignment. Members of the Horde get access to the Shaman class and members of the Alliance get the Mage class. Skyborne from either faction can be Warriors, Hunters, Rogues, or Druids, and there are all-new druid forms exclusive to Skyborne characters.

Existing races are also getting access to classes they haven’t had before. It’s now possible to create a Dwarf Shaman, Undead Paladin, Human Hunter, Gnome Priest, Troll Warlock, and Orc Mage. And you’re encouraged to try out more of these classes thanks to the Legacy System, a new account-wide progression system that provides benefits for leveling up alts.

This system introduces Legacy Points, which you can gain by completing Legacy Challenges. The challenges include things like reaching level thresholds in a class or tradeskill, attaining ranks in PvP, exploring the world map, completing groups of dungeons, and more. You can complete these challenges as multiple alts, and the Legacy Points are shared across all your characters.

You can then spend the Legacy Points for upgrades in three types of talent tree: Professions, Adventure, and Resourcefulness. The available upgrades are numerous and diverse, including things like boosting your odds of finding rare materials when gathering, regaining health and mana from kills, and eliminating the reagent requirements of class abilities.

These upgrades are character-specific, so you can spend the points for each of your alts separately and have them focus on different things. Each character can gain up to 29 Legacy Points but is limited to spending 16, so this system doesn’t require alts. You can still make use of it on just one character, but the shared point pool encourages using multiple characters.

We’re just scratching the surface of everything that’s been added. There are new dungeons, 10- and 20-player raids, skills and talents, professions content, reputations, and more. Honestly, there’s so much we couldn’t possibly list all of it here. And there’s lots more on the way, with Blizzard promising there will be regular content updates and patches for years to come.

Those updates won’t just be for endgame content, either. The plan is to release new zones, dungeons, storylines, and other content across all levels. So there’s another reason to level up some alts: You’ll get to see new places and things that weren’t available before.

On top of all the content additions, WoW: Forever also has plenty of visual upgrades. Updates to lighting, water, and other effects have clearly improved the look of the world while still retaining its original art style. That includes new global illumination, volumetric fog and sun rays, flowing water that catches the light, shadows cast by the terrain, and more stark lighting changes as the in-world day progresses.

All of these updates and additions make it clear that Blizzard views WoW: Forever as a third pillar in the franchise, standing next to the Modern and Classic versions of the game. It isn’t simply a rehash of what’s come before, it’s an update that keeps the spirit of the original game intact while finding new ways to update and expand on it.

You don’t need a separate subscription for WoW: Forever, you can play it with your sub to the base game or Game Time. It launches worldwide on November 4 and is available to pre-purchase now, so get ready to create your own story in Azeroth.

To celebrate the launch, Blizzard is hosting a real-life escape game competition in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. WoW: Forever presents Escape Together will bring together some fan-favorite streamers and cosplayers from both the Horde and the Alliance to battle it out in a series of head-to-head challenges before facing their final test together: an escape room inspired by the iconic Scarlet Monastery.

The experience will be streamed Friday, October 23 at 10 a.m. PDT on the official Warcraft Twitch channel. Viewers can tune in to see which faction brings home victory.

articles.title: The World Series comes to Milwaukee: who benefits, who's not so lucky
articles.summary: What a time to live in Milwaukee. With maybe the exception of the Bucks championship, the city hasn't had this kind of buzz in nearly 50 years.
articles.body:
Milwaukee is hosting a World Series. That's a sentence that hasn't been written in nearly 50 years and for some the excitement is palpable, and for others there's a nervous uncertainty.

The Milwaukee Brewers are facing the Tampa Bay Rays and Games 1 and 2 are scheduled for Oct. 23 and 24 at American Family Field. Many people and businesses throughout the city are feeling like winners in this playoff run, but there are a few places and events that are missing out on the fun.

Here is a look at who got lucky with the arrival of the World Series, and those who are seeing the big payoff.

What a time to live in Milwaukee. With maybe the exception of the 2021 Milwaukee Bucks NBA championship , the city hasn't had this kind of buzz in nearly 50 years. The World Series is putting Milwaukee on an international stage and generating an unexpected economic boost.

An estimate from Visit Milwaukee says Games 1 and 2 will generate $10 million to $12 million of economic impact . That is coming after early rounds of the playoffs brought in roughly $3.55 million per home game to city businesses .

Lucky: Milwaukee Brewers (duh!) and World Series merchandise

Fans have waited 44 years to get new World Series gear and they have been flocking to stores to grab what they can .

The MLB Shop, Dick's Sporting Goods, Rally House and Lids all promptly released the collection of championship series gear after the Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers.

But none of this would be happening if this team didn't put together this magical run to the World Series to give fans and the city this moment .

If you want to go to a World Series game but don't have a ticket yet be prepared to pay more than a ticket the Super Bowl . The most expensive ticket has been as much as $15,000.

"Demand for postseason tickets has been extraordinarily high, and the inventory of seats for individual purchase for possible World Series games at American Family Field will be extremely limited," Rick Schlesinger, the Brewers' president of business operations, said in an Oct. 15 statement.

Who would've known 11 years ago that putting $1,000 down for a ticket redeemable at any time for any Brewer game would be the bargain of the decade.

In 2015 the Brewers sold 1,000 "timeless tickets" to fans that they could use at any time in the future. For many fans, they held onto that ticket and are now cashing in on the promise. But some fans were upset with the location of the seats for the timeless ticket and the Brewers have been working with customers to accommodate them .

Lucky: Sports bars, restaurants and watch parties

Being able to celebrate this team with groups of strangers in community is one of the unique things about fandom.

And when the Brewers are on the road or if fans can't get a ticket at home, there have been plenty of bars and restaurants that have offered places for fans to gather and nervously cheer on the team .

The unlucky but dealing with it cheerfully

World Series games scheduled in Milwaukee Oct. 23 and 24 are affecting attendance and ticket sales for local performing arts groups with shows on those dates. But they're celebrating with the rest of Milwaukee and working out ticket exchanges with customers.

Unlucky: Milwaukee Bucks, Wisconsin Badgers

The Milwaukee Bucks started the season with a loss on the road against the Washington Wizards 128-116. And the Bucks have their home opener against the Chicago Bulls on Oct. 23, the same day as Game 1 of the World Series.

But Bucks were able to move the game from 7 p.m. to 3 p.m. and put out a statement saying:

"The Brewers' return to the World Series for the first time in 44 years is a special moment for Milwaukee and sports fans across Wisconsin. Congratulations to the Brewers and the entire organization on this tremendous achievement, and we'll be cheering them on as they begin their World Series run. The Bucks are proud to move our home opener to 3 p.m. in recognition of this historic occasion and thank the NBA for making this schedule change possible."

Milwaukee Repertory Theater has three different productions running on Oct. 23 and 24. Both nights are shaping up as low attendance, a Rep spokeswoman reported in an email.

The Rep's ticket exchange policy is "fairly lenient if they do it in advance," she said. No customer holding tickets has asked to cancel a ticket or for a refund, she said. Call the Rep box office at (414) 224-9490 for details.

"At this point it is mostly business as usual for us. Nothing special planned, except rooting for the Brewers!," she concluded.

The Milwaukee Symphony Orchestra has classical subscription concerts scheduled Oct. 23 and 24. In an email message, a symphony spokeswoman said the games are affecting ticket sales for those concerts. "We're seeing an uptick in exchange requests, but relatively few cancellations at this point," she said.

Purchased MSO tickets are non-refundable, but ticketholders can exchange them for other eligible classics or pops concerts in the current season. That exchange service is free for subscribers; there's a minimal handling free for other ticketholders, she said. Ticket exchanges must be made in advance and customers must have the new date selected at time of exchange. Call (414) 291-7605 for details.

"As fans ourselves, we understand and share in the excitement of a moment 44 years in the making," the spokeswoman said. "Our focus is on being available to patrons, answering questions, and making sure they understand their options if their plans change."

The touring musical "Jersey Boys" is at the Marcus through Oct. 25, with performances at 7:30 p.m. Oct. 23 and 24 that conflict with the Brewers' World Series games.

"New ticket sales for Friday Oct. 23 rd and Saturday Oct. 24 th have slowed down, understandably, and we are still promoting group and single tickets for all performances," a Marcus spokeswoman said in an email message.

"Thankfully, we benefit from having a 6-day run of the show with 8 total performances that enables us to process each exchange request to attend a different performance while maintaining customer-first service," she said.

"We could not be more excited that the Brewers are in the World Series," the Marcus spokeswoman said. To underline that, the venue plans to have "themed concessions" for those performances.

Tie: Some Pabst Theater Group events becoming World Series watch parties

The Pabst Theater Group - which operates local venues Miller High Life Theatre, the Riverside Theater, the Pabst Theater, Turner Hall Ballroom, Vivarium and The Fitzgerald - has 15 events scheduled on confirmed World Series game days through Oct. 27, and up to six more Oct. 28 to 31 that could face off against additional games in the series if needed.

Several performances will continue as planned opposite World Series games - including Buena Vista Orchestra at the Pabst Oct. 23; Milo Rossi at the Pabst Oct. 24; Vincent Neil Emerson at Vivarium Oct. 24; All Them Witches at Turner Hall Oct. 26; The Parables Tour with Father Mike Schmitz Oct. 27 at Miller; and Old Crow Medicine Show at the Pabst Oct. 27.

But some events are incorporating the World Series into the night, Pabst Theater Group Chief Marketing Officer Lennora Jules confirmed. The game will be shown on TVs inside the Riverside Theater during the first two nights of Widespread Panic's annual sold-out residency, with the game also shown at the street parties before the shows. Buckfest at Turner Hall Oct. 23 and 24 will have screens showing the game. And a Rod Tuffcurls and the Bench Press concert at Vivarium Oct. 23 is now a World Series Game One watch party, with the band now scheduled to perform after the game ends.

Unlucky: World Series a 'disaster' for clubs like Shank Hall

Peter Jest, owner of Shank Hall , candidly suggests the Brewers World Series run is "a disaster" for local venue operators with previously planned events.

"When you're a small club and depend on 20 or 30 tickets to make the difference and the Brewers are in the playoffs, that's really going to affect it," Jest said. "But I've been promoting (concerts) for 43 years and its never happened. ... It's good for the city and they're a fun team to watch."

Shank Hall has already made some adjustments. Chicago-based blues band Cash Box Kings have postponed a concert planned for Oct. 23, due to the conflict with Game One. A performance of "Nosferatu Undead" on Oct. 27 during game four has moved up its start time to 6 p.m. so concertgoers can still catch some of the 7 p.m. game.

A concert with Rockford, Ill.-based Miles Nielsen scheduled for Oct. 30 will move to January if Game Six in the World Series that night is needed, Jest said. An Oct. 24 show with three touring bands, led by In Her Own Words, will have to proceed as planned due to their routing, with Jest saying they'll hope for the best.

Nevertheless, this has been exciting to watch for the Brewers fan, whose gotten in on the celebrations at Shank Hall with a picture of his parrot Echo holding up a Brewers pennant that's currently on the marquee.

articles.title: Someone hacked the Switch 2 by using an old game and AI
articles.summary: A modder who goes by “pepsipu” demonstrated a Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak that let them play a custom version of Mario Kart World.
articles.body: The Nintendo Switch 2 has apparently been jailbroken, and a modder has already shown the console running a custom version of Mario Kart World featuring new playable characters like Cinnamoroll, the red Angry Bird, Peter Griffin, and Steve from Minecraft. [Media: OpenAI’s Codex helped make this “ns2jb” jailbreak, according to Sammy Hajhamid, aka “pepsipu.” It’s a software-only, tethered jailbreak, which, in this case, means that you’ll have to run it from a game every time you turn the console on for it to work. This exploit requires the game SmileBASIC 4, which lets users program and play games (though another modder claims that the title is “not strictly needed”). This jailbreak still seems extremely complex for most people, and its full impact isn’t clear yet; users on the Switch 2 hacks subreddit are debating how big of a deal it actually is. Still, this could mark the beginning of a string of exploits for the Switch 2, especially if modders use AI to help.

articles.title: Magic’s Foundations Commander Precons Are in Stock at Amazon for MSRP — But There’s a Catch
articles.summary: Amazon is selling MTG's rare Foundations precons again for MSRP, but there's a catch.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering's new Foundations Commander decks launched alongside the current set, Reality Fracture, and are intended to offer a nice “on-ramp” for new players to jump into the format.

There are five mono-colored decks to collect, and while $30 a pop is a great deal, they’ve been tough to find for MSRP — or at all, depending on where you look.

Thankfully, Amazon has restocked the lot , but there is a catch: You’ll need to buy a bundle of all five. Sadly, you’ll need to pay over the odds to buy them piecemeal, which is admittedly an annoyance if you’ve managed to grab one or two already.

MTG’s Foundation Decks Are Back To MSRP In This Bundle

Despite an MSRP of $30, they’re climbing a little; some of these decks have been reaching as high as $60 (we see you, Tramplesaurus Rex).

Whether we’ve had a fresh print run or not (we’ve asked Wizards of the Coast and are awaiting confirmation either way), it seems more product has made it to store shelves.

The best part is that you can’t really go wrong with any of them. Reign of Dragons is a fun, aggressive deck that’s all about dragons in red, while Wretched Ranks is ripe for upgrades but still fun to build an army of zombies with.

Keen Engineering will teach you the fun of mono-blue (I use that loosely) by having you outmaneuver your foes, and Calling All Angels is a surprisingly powerful precon that’s unsurprisingly all about angels.

So, what about Tramplesaurus Rex ? This mono-green behemoth is all about big creatures that swing for big damage. It’s not the most technical of decks, but there are some handy mana ramp cards that’ll slot into any other deck that has access to green. Sadly, it’s still up for $79.95 (via a third-party seller), and I can’t say enough how you should NOT PAY THAT.

As for whether they’re worth buying or not, that depends on how much you’re paying and where you are in your Magic: The Gathering journey. There are alternate arts here for each of the five Commanders, but other than that, each deck is just reprints that you might be happy with - or they might not be for you.

As we said back when these were announced, Starter Decks for Commander are not a new notion, but they’ve not been printed in so long that those ones climbed in price in the years since.

For more on Magic: The Gathering, be sure to check out Reality Fracture’s priciest cards , as well as all we know about the Warhammer 40K Commander decks seeing a reprint .

articles.title: LEGO Disney Sets Are Hitting All-Time Low Prices on Amazon Right Now
articles.body:
We're almost at the end of the year, which means LEGO is starting to offload its extra stock and " retiring soon " sets through various sales. Magical, I know. In just the past few days, Amazon has dropped prices on a range of LEGO Disney sets, including adult-oriented sets from the LEGO Ideas line and toddler-friendly LEGO Duplo builds.

Any of these sets would make a great winter activity that nets you a toy or decoration, but they could also be top-tier gifts for the Disney fan in your life . Speaking of, we're also seeing discounts on the 2026 LEGO Advent Calendars , including the Disney Princess variant.

LEGO Disney Sets Getting Big Discounts on Amazon

LEGO Disney Princess Advent Calendar 2026

LEGO Disney Frozen Olaf and Bruni’s Picnic Fun

LEGO Disney Frozen Elsa’s Ice Castle & Snow Ride Adventure

The biggest price drop in the bunch is a whopping 55% off the Kakamora Barge set, which released alongside Moana 2 and will soon be retired by LEGO . In addition to the barge itself, the 572-piece set includes a Maui build and a Moana minifigure.

Moana is frankly the main star of the deals, which also include lowest-ever prices on the smaller Kakamora and Heihei sets. The other big Disney Princess franchise seeing price drops is Frozen, with discounts on two versions of Elsa’s Ice Castle as well as an Olaf set.

For more experienced builders, the LEGO Ideas Luxo Jr. set, also known as the Pixar lamp, has dropped back down to its lowest price ever at $43. We had the chance to build this set ourselves , with reviewer Myles Obenza finding the build surprisingly intricate despite its smaller piece count. He also enjoyed the set’s “small references to classic Pixar films like Toy Story, Finding Nemo, Ratatouille, The Incredibles, and Up.”

Sally’s Flowerpot from The Nightmare Before Christmas collection has been sitting at an all-time low for a while now, but I’m of the opinion it would make a great Halloween decoration. Unfortunately, the full Nightmare Before Christmas build continues to be out of stock at most retailers, including the LEGO Store .

Will LEGO Prices Drop Lower on Black Friday?

We’re in the season of never-ending deals, which can make it hard to know when exactly you’re getting the best possible price. No one wants to pick up a discount only to watch a LEGO set's price drop even further the next day. That said, most of the sets listed above are at their lowest-ever price, and am confident those prices won’t be dropping any lower.

As I've learned from IGN’s resident LEGO expert Chris Reed , a 20% discount is pretty standard for a LEGO set, while anything above 30% off is a steal. You can also use price-tracking tools like camelcamelcamel to ensure you’re getting the best possible price.

It all feels very Mass Effect, with humans and aliens species mingling together, cuts to brief action sequences, and a cameo from a prominent character from the original trilogy. The trailer ends with a title: Mass Effect: Universe. [Media: It seems like the real deal. Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier says it is a “a real trailer of the Mass Effect game that BioWare was developing up until its closure yesterday.” IGN says it has verified the trailer is legitimate. Even though this new game has been canceled, Amazon is reportedly still working on its Mass Effect TV show for Prime Video, so there may yet be more stories to see in the Mass Effect franchise.

articles.title: Delta can turn the iPhone Duo into your favorite folding handheld
articles.summary: The Delta gaming emulator has been upgraded with a plethora of new goodies and support updates, which includes optimizing it for Apple’s iPhone Duo
articles.body: The Delta gaming emulator has been upgraded with a plethora of new goodies and support updates, which includes optimizing it for Apple’s iPhone Duo. Delta 2.0 also introduces Sega Genesis games, animated controller skins, custom Pokémon DLC experiences, and a new UI that was built around supporting Liquid Glass. Adding support for the iPhone Duo is an obvious standout here — if you looked at Apple’s flagship foldable and wondered how well it could emulate Nintendo DS games, this update was made with you in mind. Delta app creator Riley Testut told The Verge that Delta 2.0 optimizes controller skins for “every pose in both portrait and landscape,” and that you can still use split-view multitasking features alongside running other apps. Folding the Duo also puts your emulated DS games into sleep mode, just like closing the lid display of a real DS would. [Image: Here are a few more examples showing how DElta can be formatted on the iPhone Duo. That split app view on the right would tickle my ADHD brain. Similar love has been given to the newly added support for Sega Genesis games, which comes with new iPhone and iPad controller skins that “recreate the classic Genesis controller look.” There’s also a DLC feature which adds “custom in-game experiences for classic Pokémon games,” including event items, rare pokémon, and more. Testut says this will support all mainline Pokémon games released for the Game Boy Advance, with the first DLC coming “soon,” and that it was developed by the Pokémon ROM hacking community without any use of AI tools. Delta 2.0 has some experimental features too, including support for Epilogue’s GB/SN Operator gadgets, which now allow you to play your old Nintendo cartridges on your iPhone or iPad. Another experiment is Custom Filters, which change the appearance of your games using a filter overlay. You can choose from a set of defaults, such as a CRT-inspired filter, or import your own to experience games exactly how you first remember playing them. The app’s UI has been overhauled for Apple’s Liquid Glass design language, which fully adapts to all screen sizes across iPhones, iPads, and the iPhone Duo, giving default artwork a light, glassy look. There’s also new animated controller skins (with support for third-party designs), new pages for “recents” and “favorites” in the game library, new settings options, and more. Outside of actual gameplay perks, Delta is adding global support for in-app purchases, which appears as a new “Become a Patron” option. This release also marks the first time that Delta will release to the EU App Store, making it available globally on Apple’s app marketplace alongside AltStore PAL in supported regions.

articles.title: Cormac McCarthy’s The Road Is on Sale for $1.99 on Kindle
articles.body:
Wouldn’t it be nice to curl up with a good book right about now? If you use the Kindle ebook platform, you can pick up one of my all-time favorite novels on sale right now for just $1.99. It’s The Road, by Cormac McCarthy, and you can get it at Amazon for barely any money at all. It tells the story of a father and his son trying to survive in a post-apocalyptic America that’s been scorched of nearly all other life.

The Road, by Cormac McCarthy (Kindle ebook)

McCarthy is known for having dense, poetic prose, but he’s at his most readable in The Road. The book is comprised of many short sections, often just a paragraph long, with plenty of white space between each one. Here’s a scene-setting excerpt from near the beginning:

“With the first gray light he rose and left the boy sleeping and walked out to the road and squatted and studied the country to the south. Barren, silent, godless. He thought the month was October but he wasnt sure. He hadnt kept a calendar for years. They were moving south. There’d be no surviving another winter here.”

Notice the lack of apostrophes in some of the words. McCarthy famously doesn’t use quotation marks, either, but you almost always know who’s speaking. The sparse punctuation and the occasional unusual word choice create a unique tone in all of his work.

But whereas some of his other books, like Blood Meridian (often considered his masterpiece), are almost plotless and endlessly violent, The Road tells a simpler story of survival that's easy to follow. It has characters you can root for, even if a major victory is just them discovering unopened canned food in an abandoned cellar.

The Road won the 2007 Pulitzer Prize for fiction and went on to be turned into a movie starring Viggo Mortensen (the book is way better). It's one of his most popular novels; others include No Country for Old Men and All the Pretty Horses.

McCarthy was famously reclusive, rarely agreeing to be interviewed, but Oprah picked The Road for her book club and scored one of those rare interviews .

Cormac McCarthy died in 2023, but he carved out a singular voice in American fiction. I’ve read about half of his books, and of those, I’d say The Road is by far the best entry point into his work. I can't recommend it highly enough, especially for $1.99.

articles.title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Says Gen Z is 'Tired' of Unoriginal Stories in Hollywood
articles.summary: Speaking on the Kyle Buchanan Show, Inde Navarrette gave her impression of Gen Z’s renewed interest in going to the movies and what kinds of pictures they’re keen on seeing following the success of Backrooms and Obsession over the summer.
articles.body:
Speaking on the Kyle Buchanan Show, Inde Navarrette gave her impression of Gen Z’s renewed interest in going to the movies and what kinds of pictures they’re keen on seeing, following the success of Backrooms and Obsession over the summer.

It’s safe to say that Inde Navarrette has a bright future ahead of her, in no small part due to her standout performance in Curry Barker’s Obsession . The movie quickly became one of the most profitable indie flicks ever made and brought oodles of younger viewers to theaters, earning rave reviews from audiences and critics alike.

This, alongside the success of 21-year-old Kane Parson’s Backrooms , have highlighted a growing trend among moviegoers; young audiences are keen on seeing original stories brought to the screen and love when studios take a chance on new talent.

Navarrette echoed this sentiment during her interview on the Kyle Buchanan Show , where the host asked her what Gen Z wants to see on the silver screen.

“I think Gen Z just wants to go to something that they don’t feel like they’re being sold,” she answered. “I think that maybe we are tired constantly of having ads in movies or production placement and all of these things. We understand it’s fundamental, right? We grew up with commercials that are fun that we still quote, like State Farm and Aflac, or whatever. It’s kind of fun. But we don’t want to be sold. We want original stories.”

“Just because we’re living in the time of technology doesn’t mean we’re not living a human life or feeling human experiences. I’m happy Obsession brought that to the table. We want originality and authenticity, and we want to feel,” she continued.

Navarrette’s remarks speak to the rise in popularity for horror films and smaller projects lately. In fact, Backrooms kicked off an industry-wide rush to snatch up the rights to internet copypasta IPs to greenlight films for the likes of The Mandela Catalogue (directed by Spielberg, himself), The SCP Foundation, and even Siren Head , with none other than Zach Cregger onboard to produce.

The Obsession actress isn’t wrong; as pointed out by Variety , a study from Fandango found that Gen Z is the largest demographic of moviegoers right now, with 87% — alongside 82% of millennials — going to theaters to see at least one movie over the last year.

Fandango executive vice president Jerramy Hainline remarked on this data, saying, “While there has been a perception that Gen Z is less engaged with theatrical moviegoing, our data shows that their momentum has been building. What’s especially notable is how strongly they value the shared, communal aspect of the experience, reinforcing that theaters continue to play an important role as a social destination for younger audiences.”

Navarrette is now pivoting toward a much larger project, having been confirmed to play Rogue in Marvel’s X-Men reboot. She’s also keen on voicing a character in a Resident Evil game , and said she studied anime like Jujutsu Kaisen and Demon Slayer to better understand scriptwriting and storytelling.

articles.title: ‘Now You’re Pushing It’ — Debra Wilson Drew the Line at the Wolverine Devs Scanning Her Tattoos Into the Game
articles.summary: In a recent interview with GameSpot, actor Debra Wilson, who you might recognize from Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, Wolfenstein: The New Colossus, or God of War Ragnarok, said she’s sick of seeing her face in video games. The actor said the developers choose it and she’d rather play characters that don’t resemble her.
articles.body:
In a recent interview with GameSpot , actor Debra Wilson, who you might recognize from Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order , Wolfenstein: The New Colossus , or God of War Ragnarok , said she’s sick of seeing her face in video games. The actor said the developers choose it and she’d rather play characters that don’t resemble her.

“I don’t necessarily dig it,” Wilson said. “Because I might as well be doing it on camera. It's hard to suspend your disbelief. There are people who are like, ‘Oh my God, she's in every f***ing game. What the f***?’ And there are other people like, ‘I am sick of looking at her face because I just want to play the game and not think of Debra Wilson.’”

It’s become a bit of a meme in gaming communities, with players complaining that they’re being taken out of the experience because they’ve seen Wilson’s face pop up.

“I don't blame them because I feel the same,” she said. “Why do you have to show my face? Amanda Waller in Suicide Squad, Grace Walker in Wolfenstein: The New Colossus, and now with the new Wolverine game coming out, I'm Callisto. Guess who the f*** she looks like?

“They wanted to scan my original tattoos. I was like, ‘Now you're pushing it. No, you're pushing that s**t.’ So I have been grateful for the work that has come in the video game industry where my characters are European.”

Later in the interview, she talked about how she wouldn’t want to include it as a contract stipulation because she wants artists to be able to tell stories in whatever way they like. But as an actor who’s played demons, dragons, and all sorts of other non-human entities, it doesn’t really capture what she’s capable of.

She also noted that it depends on the game. In Death Stranding 2, her likeness was used but so was almost every other actor’s.

“I am not upset at their choice to do that because everybody looks like themselves,” she said. “[Hideo Kojima] knew what he wanted. He's more than a director. He's an artist.”

Wilson recently starred as Jessica Pike in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Callisto in Marvel’s Wolverine, and did background voices in Modern Warfare 4.

articles.title: Stephen King Responds as Carrie Renewed for Second Season on Prime Video
articles.summary: Prime Video has officially renewed Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season, saying there’s “much more in store” for our favorite prom queen.
articles.body:
Prime Video has officially renewed Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season, saying there’s “much more in store” for our favorite prom queen.

Amazon announced the news today, October 22, revealing that Carrie skyrocketed to the number one spot on Prime Video across 105 countries worldwide. It’s no surprise; the show was well-received by critics and audiences alike, sparking no end of fan theories and comparisons to other adaptations of Stephen King’s debut novel.

As per a press release from Prime Video, Carrie’s story is “far from over,” and “much remains in store from Mike Flanagan and Stephen King, as new revelations will come to light, major character arcs, and plenty of shocking twists.”

"Carrie is connecting with both longtime Stephen King fans and a new generation altogether — including young adults and international audiences, with particular strength among female viewers," Amazon MGM Studios’ Head of Global Television, Peter Friedlander, said in a statement. "It speaks to the enduring power of this story and signals that Mike Flanagan's reimagining of the iconic IP has real breadth. We're excited by where he and Stephen plan to take the story."

Mike Flanagan also shared excitement to continue Carrie’s story past the original novel. “For 50 years, audiences have known and gravitated to Carrie White’s story. From the beginning, we imagined a story that goes far beyond the prom, and I’m incredibly grateful for Stephen’s trust and support in exploring what comes next,” he said.

“I can’t wait for audiences to get to see what’s down the road for Carrie White. Mike Flanagan and I are excited about what comes next. It’s bound to be thrilling,” Stephen King, who served as executive producer on the show, added.

Flanagan’s Carrie was always ripe for a second season . It notably included elements from King’s other works like The Dark Tower and Doctor Sleep, and perhaps most importantly, Carrie lives at the end, being whisked away to safety by astral projector Emaline as they flee from Adelaide and a shadowy group of fellow telekinetics with the Shine.

There’s much we don’t know about this growing storyline, and although it deviates wildly from King’s original novel, it’s being produced by the man himself, who has expressed nothing but positivity for Flanagan’s take on the source material and is clearly jazzed for a second season.

Carrie offers a modern-day retelling of the ‘74 book that resonates with 2026 viewers, portraying the harsh realities of being a student in an increasingly dangerous learning environment, current political issues, and the real impact social media has on peoples’ lives.

Carrie is available to watch on Prime Video right now. IGN scored the show an eight out of ten , with reviewer Tom Jorgensen saying: “With smart story accommodations for the social media age and a pair of stellar performances from Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan, Mike Flanagan and his team have successfully made the case for why Carrie’s story needed to be retold.”

articles.title: A Talent for Murder With Helen Mirren, Alden Ehrenreich, and Olivia Cooke Takes a Stab at Metafiction
articles.summary: A Talent for Murder review: What are you gonna do? Stab me?
articles.body:
A Talent for Murder is in theaters October 22.

Many a low-level employee has felt like a tyrannical boss or nightmare client is one inconvenience away from killing them, and have also felt the desire to do the same to them in turn. That impulse is the driving tension of A Talent for Murder , a new not-quite/not-quite-not murder mystery thriller from director Anton Corbijn.

Adapted from the Joanna Murray-Smith stage play Switzerland by the playwright herself, A Talent for Murder is a not-quite/not-quite-not chamber piece (you may notice a running theme here) about a young employee of a New York literary agency sent on a mission to Switzerland to track down famed novelist Patricia Highsmith (a fictionalized take on the real person) at her home and convince her to write one more book starring her most famous creation, Tom Ripley. Such affairs would not typically involve the threat of murder... but if they didn’t, we wouldn’t have much of a movie, now would we?

Alden Ehrenreich stars as Edward Ridgeway, who’s been ordered to get Highsmith (Helen Mirren) to sign a contract for one more Ripley book or he'll face the unemployment line. Highsmith is predictably highstrung (hah), irritable from the start, and domineering to the end. She wants nothing more to do with the talented Mr. Ripley, the suave sociopath who’s paid her bills for so long and is most known to audiences for being portrayed by a young Matt Damon in 1999. Not one to be deterred so easily, the seemingly naive Edward manages to worm his way into staying for one night at Highsmith’s hideaway house, giving himself time to see if he can pitch the plot for a new novel to the insular author, who may or may not have killed the last hapless employee saddled with the same objective. To say that there’s more to what’s going on here would be stating the obvious, but it would also, perplexingly, be overstirring the pot.

For when Edward and Highsmith reconvene to begin plotting a novel that would excite the author enough to actually write it, A Talent for Murder unspools into what actually takes up the majority of the runtime: a dramatization of the hypothetical book they’re discussing. This story within a story has some parallels to the “real life” plot, what with a young man with more ambition than he lets on charming his way into the life of a woman who’s his ticket to potential profit, and enlists Ehrenreich into a double role by playing the Ripley analogue that Edward and Highsmith are crafting. It’s a neat idea at first glance until you realize that it’s essentially like watching a narrated pitch meeting for the more straightforwardly satisfying thriller that A Talent for Murder wants to be. The metafictional conceit is a double-edged sword that winds up slashing both plotlines, ensuring the “real” story is lacking in suspense and rendering the “fake” story devoid of stakes.

That’s not to say A Talent for Murder doesn’t have its merits. Mirren and Ehrenreich have solid adversarial chemistry, and the latter acquits himself admirably playing two characters who begin to bleed into each other as the movie marches on. Olivia Cooke proves herself a reliable if somewhat unchallenged performer by the unambitiously written but fancifully named Clementine Balfour, a woman Edward meets on the train into Switzerland whom he mentally recycles into the love interest/con victim of the same name that makes for the second lead of the novel. The location cinematography from frequent Yorgos Lanthimos collaborator Robbie Ryan is gorgeous and colorful, and the film’s costume and production design is first rate. To quote a common meme, the film has “great gowns, beautiful gowns”; what it’s ultimately lacking in, sadly, is surprise.

Despite featuring two plotlines and plenty of room for intrigue, the “story with a story” concept robs the film of urgency. No matter how much murder and mayhem Edward and Highsmith’s character may get up to in his quest for Clementine’s fortune, what is actually happening is two people sitting in a room talking about a novel that does not exist. The multiple layers of abstraction result in a film that struggles to convey the looming dread that drives the best minimalist mystery fare. Typically a movie or play in this style features multiple big twists that completely recontextualize the scenario — think something like Anthony Shaffer’s Sleuth or Ira Levin’s Deathtrap. But A Talent for Murder lacks punch by never having a massive "rug pull" moment to hang its hat on.

With the caveat that I haven’t seen the play this is based on, I can’t help but feel that a significant contributor to A Talent for Murder being too leisurely for its own good is a playwright who is too precious about adapting her own material. Although this is not Murray-Smith’s first film credit, she’s not a screenwriter by trade, having spent much more time in the world of theater. The energy required for a great mystery film is similar but not identical to that needed for a compelling stage play, and that mismatch of form is the biggest anchor holding the film back, even if it’s not enough to sink it entirely.

articles.title: New Look at Avengers: Doomsday to Premiere During MLB World Series

A brand new preview for Avengers: Doomsday will debut during the MLB World Series.

The news was confirmed by the MLB itself, which noted that the exclusive sneak peek will drop during game one of the World Series. The game, which will be played by the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers, will begin tomorrow, Friday, October 23 at 8PM eastern time. They didn't give an exact time for when this preview will happen, but it wouldn't be surprising if it takes place later in the game to keep viewers watching.

Something’s coming … Tune in to World Series Game 1 for an exclusive preview of Avengers: Doomsday In theaters everywhere December 18

With that said, you can expect that this preview will likely also be released online, either through official Marvel channels or from a fan reupload. It's unclear if this is a brand-new trailer or an extended clip from the film. So far, we've gotten two trailers for Avengers: Doomsday, which have shown off the expansive cast of heroes battling Doctor Doom. We don't actually know a whole lot about the plot of the film, as Marvel has managed to keep things heavily under wraps. It's expected that Doom will cause an incursion event, which causes two different universes to collide in a catastrophic fashion.

The recent re-release of Avengers: Endgame also included new scenes , which tease some events for Doomsday. At the end of the re-release, Hulk is abducted by Doctor Doom and the TVA begin to witness the multiverse falling apart via incursions. The stakes are arguably the highest they have ever been in the Marvel universe, which should lead to a very dramatic adventure.

This new look should hopefully paint a better picture of what fans can expect when the film hits theaters. We are currently just two months away from the release of Avengers: Doomsday, which will also debut the same day as Dune Part 3. The two films are expected to duke it out at the box office, with Dune having the benefit of exclusive IMAX screens. There has been some speculation that Doomsday may get an IMAX release later , not unlike Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The film is expected to get an IMAX release in China, so there will be a version for Marvel to release in other territories if it so chooses.

Avengers: Doomsday is also expected to be the first of a two-part story, like Infinity War and Endgame. Avengers: Secret Wars is currently slated to release next December, though some fear it may be delayed, as production reportedly hasn't even properly begun . It's believed that Secret Wars will also make room for some other characters not featured in Doomsday, with some speculating that Star-Lord may make his grand return following recent comments from Chris Pratt . We'll just have to wait and see what happens, though.

Avengers: Doomsday will hit theaters on December 18.

articles.title: Tom Skerritt Dies: Alien and Top Gun Actor Was 93
articles.summary: Tom Skerritt, the rugged, mustachioed actor best known to IGN readers for his roles in Top Gun and Alien, passed away from natural causes on Wednesday at the age of 93.
articles.body:
Tom Skerritt, the rugged, mustachioed actor best known to IGN readers for his roles in Top Gun and Alien, passed away from natural causes on Wednesday at the age of 93.

“We are heartbroken by his loss,” Skerritt’s family said in a statement provided to The Hollywood Reporter .

“While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity and the love he brought into our lives. He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world and helping others find and share their own voices.”

Skerritt first gained acclaim as a film actor in director Robert Altman’s 1970 comedy M*A*S*H, where he played surgeon Duke Forrest, one of the few characters not included in the later classic TV series adaptation.

Other notable films of Skerritt’s in the 1970s include Harold and Maude, The Turning Point, Fuzz, Thieves Like Us, and Cheech & Chong’s Up in Smoke.

After initially turning down the role, Skerritt played Captain Arthur Dallas in Ridley Scott’s now classic sci-fi/horror film Alien (1979). Skerritt belonged to an ensemble that included Sigourney Weaver, Yaphet Kotto, Ian Holm, John Hurt, Harry Dean Stanton, and Veronica Cartwright. (Be sure to read Scott Collura's deep-dive interview with Tom Skerritt about the making of Alien .)

During the 1980s, Skerritt had roles in films such as The Dead Zone, Wisdom, SpaceCamp, Poltergeist III, and Steel Magnolias. But the role from that decade Skerritt best came to be remembered for is Commander Mike "Viper" Metcalf in 1986’s Top Gun. As the Commanding Office of the Top Gun program, Viper had to keep hot shot US Navy fighter pilots like Tom Cruise’s Maverick and Val Kilmer’s Iceman in check.

Skerritt’s most notable film role in the 1990s was as the father of Brad Pitt and Craig Sheffer’s character in director Robert Redford’s 1992 drama A River Runs Through It.

He later appeared in Singles, Contact, Smoke Signals, Tears of the Sun, Whiteout, and A Hologram for the King. Skerritt played himself in Seth McFarlane’s 2012 comedy Ted.

While Skerritt’s career in television goes back to the early 1960s, his most notable role on the screen was as Sheriff Jimmy Brock in the David E. Kelley-created 1992-96 series Picket Fences. Skerritt won a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series for the role. The actor also did stints on Cheers, Brothers & Sisters, Huff, and The Good Wife.

Born Thomas Roy Skerritt on August 25, 1933 in Detroit, Michigan, Skerritt was married three times and had five children. He was also a military veteran having served in the US Air Force from 1951-55.

articles.title: Young Sheldon Star Annie Potts Says She Was a ‘Little Sad’ About Jim Parsons Cameo as 'Mean and Unchanged' Sheldon in Show's Finale
articles.summary: Annie Potts, who portrayed a younger version of Sheldon’s Meemaw on Young Sheldon, revealed how she felt about the show’s finale, disagreeing with how adult Sheldon remained "mean and unchanged" in Parsons' finale cameo.
articles.body:
Annie Potts, who portrayed a younger version of Sheldon’s Meemaw on Young Sheldon, revealed how she felt about the show’s finale, disagreeing with how adult Sheldon remained "mean and unchanged" in Parsons' finale cameo.

The end of Young Sheldon — the seven-season-long Big Bang Theory Spinoff show — was rife with drama. Its abrupt ending was reportedly revealed to cast members in a Zoom call, with Potts saying she felt “blindsided” by the decision and went "full Meemaw” on the series’ producers.

She elaborated on these feelings in a book authored by Jessica Radloff titled Young Sheldon: The (Juicier-Than-Meemaw’s-Brisket) Inside Story of the Hit Comedy, where she described her reaction to Jim Parson’s cameo at the end of the final episode as a grown-up Sheldon.

According to Radloff’s book, Potts was “a little sad” about how Sheldon remained “mean and unchanged” as a character despite all the events of the prequel series.

“That broke my heart,” she told the author. “It was like, ‘Really? Still no responsibility?’ It was just selfishness. It’s just not how I wish to see Sheldon off into the world. …I thought the show could have ended [with young Sheldon] and not to the dreaded scene with Jim and Mayim as Sheldon and Amy revealing he was unchanged and unrepentant. That gave me a stomachache. It was like, ‘Who crashed our party?! Who invited you?'”

While most of the cast reportedly felt similarly burnt by the situation, Young Sheldon himself, Iain Armitage, said he was probably the only member who was actually happy that the show was finally over .

“Looking back now, it’s nostalgic-sad,” he said. “Like, I miss working at Warner Bros., I miss the crew and the people I love. I love the act of acting. I love doing it. It’s fun. But not really specific moments. More the overall thing.”

He went on to call the intense reaction to the show’s cancellation from his fellow castmates as “heavy and annoying and weird,” saying he wanted to be back in Virginia.

“I wanted to be traveling, and I’m happy to do whatever movie comes up. And my mom has always imbued me with a very healthy sense of ephemerality, and the fact that nothing good can last and everything changes, and that’s a good thing,” he continued. “I would hate to be on a show playing 23-year-old Sheldon. That would suck. I wouldn’t want to do that. So it was a perfect time to end it,” he said in the book.

A Young Sheldon spinoff series was greenlit (news that, reportedly, also blindsided the original show’s cast), focusing on Georgie and Mandy as young parents in the 90s. It was first announced in 2024 and is still running today, currently on its third season.
